basics.name: Valentinos Pariza
basics.label: PhD Researcher in Computer Vision
basics.summary: My research connects how models understand images with how they generate and edit them. Through NeCo and Franca, I worked on self-supervised vision encoders and the spatial information in their representations. I now study diffusion models for image editing, generation, and visual perception, with growing interests in multimodal learning and video. Across this work, I want to understand which visual knowledge transfers between tasks and use it to build more capable models with efficient training and adaptation.

work.name: Fundamental AI Lab, University of Technology Nuremberg (UTN)
work.summary: Research on visual representations, image editing, generation, and perception. Advisor: Prof. Yuki M. Asano.
highlights: Open Vision Banana (ongoing; manuscript in preparation): core contributor to adapting image editors for perception tasks, including segmentation. My main work covers depth and surface-normal prediction, image editing, and generation. Public release planned.
Franca: co-first author and core contributor to research ideas, implementation, training at standard and high resolutions, experiments, ablations, and writing.
RASA (part of Franca): designed and implemented the method to remove unwanted absolute-position information from visual features, and conducted its experiments and ablations.

work.name: TNO - Netherlands Organisation for Applied Scientific Research
work.summary: MSc thesis research on dense visual representations.
highlights: Developed NeCo with collaborators, improving dense visual representations with 19 hours of post-training on a single GPU in the reported setup (ICLR 2025).
Developed and released Open Hummingbird Evaluation, implementing Balažević et al.'s dense nearest-neighbor evaluation for vision encoders.

work.name: South Pole
highlights: Worked with other teams to understand matching errors, gather requirements, and identify tools we could reuse.
Built an evaluation dataset and improved product-to-category matching accuracy by 25.2 percentage points using a text transformer encoder.
Deployed the models to production using Kubernetes.

work.name: CYENS Centre of Excellence
highlights: Developed a Python library using JAX for quality-diversity optimization, more than doubling the speed of the evaluated algorithms.

work.name: Amazon Data Services Ireland
highlights: Worked with other teams to understand reporting and logging problems, identify bottlenecks, and turn their requirements into software improvements.
Built and deployed an automated reporting service, saving each employee involved approximately 8–10 hours of manual reporting per week. Also improved a Java library for accessing internal data.
Improved a real-time log analysis service and led two campaigns to improve logging practices, reducing annual costs by thousands of dollars.

work.name: Fooderloo
work.summary: Co-founded Fooderloo to help reduce food waste in Cyprus. Built the backend and database.
